title: narrate
body:
## narrate

Speak one short plain-text script with the fixed offline English (United States) eSpeak NG voice, or with one explicitly selected voice (en-gb, fr-fr or es), and publish a canonical PCM16 mono 22050 Hz WAV voiceover draft. The host captures the script bytes, refuses control characters, [[ ]] phoneme escapes, markup and text without words, runs the trusted espeak-ng with fixed arguments, and then re-synthesises the captured text in a separate process: every PCM byte must match. Choose it to create a first-pass narration to listen to, to time a script, or to feed a speech or archive step; it is synthetic, not a human recording, and a person must read the words and listen before publishing.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- The speaking rate and an optional voice are the only authored synthesis choices. Without voice the fixed English (United States) voice speaks; with voice only en-us, en-gb, fr-fr or es are accepted. Pitch, amplitude, voice names or paths, variants, flags, SSML, phoneme codes, language detection and translation are rejected, not passed through.
- The script must be plain words: control characters (including tabs, carriage returns and form feeds), [[ ]] phoneme escapes, SSML or other markup, and text with no letter or digit are refused with the offending code point; nothing is silently rewritten. The synthesizer may still expand numbers and abbreviations or ignore characters, so read the words as well as listening.
- Verification needs the same trusted espeak-ng 1.52.0 with matching native data (--espeakng for run, or SCHEMAXIS_ESPEAKNG or a stored espeakng location for verify). A different build or voice data can change the samples and fail an older proof. Success proves consistent derivation only, not intelligibility, pronunciation, accent or accessibility.
- A voice speaks the script as written by its own rules: Schemaxis does not detect or check the script language, translate it or correct it, so choose the voice that matches the language of the words (for example fr-fr for French text). The voice label is the one the runtime lists for that name, not a certificate of the accent or pronunciation you will hear.

Native binding: `espeak-ng --version; espeak-ng --voices=LANGUAGE; espeak-ng -vVOICE -sRATE -p50 -a100 -b1 -w native.wav -f captured.txt (eSpeak NG 1.52.0; VOICE is en-us by default or for the explicit en-us, and for the explicit en-gb, fr-fr or es the fixed identifier of its native voice file, gmw/en, roa/fr or roa/es, with the fixed LANGUAGE query of the selected voice); a fresh verification run repeats the same fixed commands in a private directory`. Output kind: `["file","text"]`.

Inputs: none.

| Option | Meaning | Type / constraints | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | The script to speak, written directly in the document: plain words, 1 to 1024 Unicode code points and at most 8 KiB of UTF-8. Use this for a short line or two; line feeds separate lines. It is captured exactly as written. Author exactly one of text and source. | `{"type":"string","minLength":1,"maxLength":1024}` | omitted |
| `source` | Choose one absolute local UTF-8 .txt file holding the script, at most 1024 code points and 8 KiB, or bind a verified text or file artifact from an earlier step (for example a whisper.cpp transcript.txt). The file bytes are captured before synthesis and decide scheduler reuse. Author exactly one of text and source. | `{"type":"string","minLength":1,"maxLength":4096}` | omitted |
| `rateWpm` | Speaking rate in approximate words per minute, from 120 (slow and deliberate) to 240 (brisk). It scales how fast the fixed voice speaks; it does not change pitch or voice. Use the default for general narration, slow it down for instructions or clarity, speed it up for terse announcements. | `{"type":"integer","minimum":120,"maximum":240}` | `175` |
| `voice` | Optionally choose which of four fixed offline eSpeak NG voices speaks the script: en-us (English, United States), en-gb (English, Great Britain), fr-fr (French, France) or es (Spanish, Spain). It selects the voice only: the script is not translated, language-checked or corrected, so pick the voice that matches the language of the words. Leave it out for the original English (United States) voice, whose plans and proofs are unchanged. | `{"type":"enum","values":["en-us","en-gb","fr-fr","es"]}` | omitted |
